question: Out of every 1,000 people on Earth, how many work in agriculture — farming, fishing, or forestry?
answer_explanation: Agriculture employs more people than any other sector on Earth. Most are smallholder farmers in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa, where farming remains the primary livelihood for a large share of the population. In wealthy, mechanised nations the figure drops to under 2% of the workforce.

relationship_fact.text: More than 90% of the world's farms are smallholdings under 2 hectares — most are in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa, where agriculture remains the primary livelihood for billions

temporal_fact.text: Over the past three decades, South Asia's agricultural workforce contracted significantly to two-thirds of its 1990 baseline. By contrast, sub-Saharan Africa experienced a much more gradual transition, with its 2023 farming workforce retaining five-sixths of its 1990 level.

scale_fact.text: In South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa, roughly half of all workers are in agriculture — compared to under 5% in wealthy nations, reflecting how mechanisation has transformed farming in richer countries
